QuestionStmt.S: Calculate the change in internal energy of the system if 20 kJ of work is done on the system and it releases 10 kJ of heat in a particular reaction.

Solution.S:
According to the **First Law of Thermodynamics**, the change in internal energy ($\Delta U$) is given by:
$$\Delta U = q + w$$

Where:
$q$ is the heat absorbed by the system.
$w$ is the work done on the system.

Given:
Work done on the system, $w = +20$ kJ

System releases heat, so $q = -10$ kJ (since heat is released by the system)

Substitute the values:
$$\Delta U = (-10) + (20)$$
$$\Delta U = 10 \, \text{kJ}$$

Final Answer:
Option B: 10 kJ
